PullRequest.Title: agentHost: Restrict Codex default permissions to workspace
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- define VS Code-owned Codex permission profiles that grant workspace access plus minimal system runtime reads while denying arbitrary filesystem reads outside the workspace
- select the effective profile across thread start, turns, forks, resumes, backing chats, multi-root workspaces, additional directories, and Agent Merge
- preserve the existing three presets: Default and Auto-Review use workspace-scoped access, while Full Access remains unrestricted

Fixes #334925

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- focused ESLint on the five changed files
- 61 focused Codex unit tests
- `git diff --check`
- live Code OSS verification of all three picker modes:
  - Default: workspace read/write succeeds; `/etc/passwd` is denied
  - Auto-Review: workspace profile with auto-review routing; `/etc/passwd` is denied
  - Full Access: unrestricted profile; `/etc/passwd` succeeds
- verified the bundled app-server keeps the explicit workspace profile active with legacy `sandbox_mode` in both user config and launch overrides

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold startup account probe and first persistent Codex activation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A cold account probe or first explicit Codex use waits for proxy startup, Codex subprocess spawn, and the initialize IPC handshake. The diff only appends four fixed permission-profile command-line overrides before that spawn.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start the local Codex proxy service
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per raw app-server connection, unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same proxy start completed before every raw connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks subprocess launch on cold startup or activation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Spawn the Codex app-server with command-line configuration
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One spawn per cold/transient/replacement connection; the diff adds four constant-size -c pairs to that spawn.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same process was spawned with provider, feature, and telemetry overrides; only the fixed argument payload is larger.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks cold process initialization, but does not add a spawn or scale argument construction with user input.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initialize request per spawned process, unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One initialize request followed every spawn.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed four-profile launch configuration per spawned app-server process; independent of workspace size, thread count, and history size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Startup probe is one transient process; on-demand work is sequenced, and persistent connection creation is coalesced by the existing starting promise. The diff does not change these limits.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold paths spawn and parse launch configuration once per process. Warm activated sessions reuse the existing ready process, so the new overrides are not rebuilt per turn.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the subprocess/IPC path and cardinality are unchanged; repository code directly shows fixed argument construction and existing connection coalescing.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No measurements quantify native parsing of the four extra constant strings, but their fixed size and once-per-process placement rule out realistic scaling or repeated hot-path regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the diff adds only constant launch payload to an already expensive cold boundary and does not alter process count, initialization requests, or concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create and materialize a fresh session or additional backing chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Materialization performs existing MCP/customization filesystem work, ensures the shared process, then waits for one thread/start IPC. The diff replaces the sandbox field with a permission-profile id and may serialize explicit runtime roots for single-root workspace-write sessions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh session MCP discovery and build customization launch data
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing work over current workspace roots once during materialization; unaffected by permission-profile selection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same MCP discovery/customization work occurred before computing and sending sandbox settings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completes before thread/start and remains on the existing materialization critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send thread/start to the Codex app-server
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one request per successful fresh/backing thread creation, unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One thread/start carried sandbox mode and, for multi-root sessions, runtime roots; it now carries a short profile id and explicit effective roots where required.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks creation until the app-server returns the thread id.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Workspace roots plus configured additional directories after path deduplication; normally one or a small number of roots.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each materialization issues one thread/start request on the shared app-server. The diff adds no loop, fan-out, queue, or new request.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The shared app-server is reused when warm. Session configuration is read from in-memory state; permission selection has no cache and is constant-time. Root normalization is linear in the small root list.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in unchanged host-side request count and O(root-count) serialization; low evidence for any additional native cost, so no regression mechanism is established.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The app-server implementation is external to this repository, so internal handling cost of an explicit single workspace root is not measured. No repository evidence shows that setting runtime roots triggers scanning or extra boundary calls.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: one IPC remains one IPC, local work is bounded by the effective root list, and no expensive per-root host boundary was introduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send ordinary turns, including multi-root, additional-directory, network, and Agent Merge modes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After existing model/customization preparation, each non-compact prompt constructs turn options and waits for one turn/start IPC acknowledgement; turn execution then proceeds asynchronously. The changed helper selects a permission profile and rebuilds the effective runtime root list.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send turn/start with prompt, profile, and runtime roots
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC request per ordinary user turn, unchanged; compact turns use their separate unchanged request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each ordinary turn already sent one turn/start containing approval settings, a sandbox policy, and effective writable/runtime roots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The acknowledgement is on the prompt-send critical path, but only field shape changes from sandboxPolicy to permissions/runtimeWorkspaceRoots.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of workspace roots and additional directories after deduplication, once per user turn; prompt size and model execution dominate and are unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new parallel work is introduced. Each invocation sends one turn/start request; connection creation remains coalesced, and the diff does not add boundary fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configuration reads are in-memory state lookups. Root/profile values are recomputed per turn, as sandbox policy and writable roots were before; there is no newly defeated cache or retained collection.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the direct call path that previous and changed implementations both compute root-dependent permission data once and send one IPC request per turn.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact native permission matching cost is unavailable, but profile ids and root lists are small and no changed host operation scales with files, messages, or history.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: no additional synchronous I/O, IPC, serialization fan-out, or retained state is introduced on the turn path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resume a restored or reloaded session after configuration or connection changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A resume refreshes existing MCP/customization data, may send the existing conditional unsubscribe, then waits for one thread/resume IPC. The diff adds in-memory permission resolution and three scalar permission fields to that existing request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh MCP discovery/customization information before resume
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per resume attempt over workspace roots, pre-existing and unaffected by the new permission calculations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same discovery and customization preparation occurred before thread/resume.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Conditionally unsubscribe and then resume the Codex thread
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero or one unsubscribe plus one resume per attempt, unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same conditional unsubscribe and one thread/resume request were issued; the resume payload lacked explicit approval/reviewer/profile overrides.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks the next turn until resume completes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective workspace-root and additional-directory count, plus existing MCP/customization configuration; no dependence newly added on thread history size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-session resumePromise coalesces concurrent resume demand; replacement retries are pre-existing. The diff does not change retry or unsubscribe behavior.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm loaded sessions avoid resume. A cold/reload path reads configuration from in-memory session state and serializes roots once; existing MCP discovery cache and signatures are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that added work is bounded local validation and serialization and that boundary cardinality, retry, and coalescing behavior are unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No benchmark quantifies validation of the small session config object, but it is synchronous in-memory work once per resume attempt and materially smaller than existing filesystem and IPC work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the diff does not add a boundary or increase resume frequency, and per-resume local work is small and bounded.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: Fork preparation reads source state and may copy a managed working directory, then waits for one thread/fork IPC and an existing conditional rollback. The diff validates the already-read merged config once and sends a permission profile instead of sandbox mode.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copy a managed source working directory for an isolated fork when applicable
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One recursive copy only for the pre-existing managed-directory case, unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same recursive copy occurred before thread/fork.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send thread/fork and, when needed, thread/rollback
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One fork plus at most one rollback, unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same requests were sent with sandbox mode rather than a named permission profile.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both existing requests are on the fork critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Source history determines existing fork-boundary work and rollback count; permission work scales only with the small configuration object and not with history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One fork request per fork operation, with one conditional rollback as before. No new parallelism or fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Source configuration is read once from in-memory state and merged once. The added schema validation is per fork and retains no state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the direct before/after call path that expensive boundary count and history processing are unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Schema object size and fork prevalence are not measured, but the added local validation is bounded and no history-wide or filesystem work was added.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the diff changes permission payload representation without adding fork I/O, IPC, or collection-wide repeated work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files and all diff hunks. Traced cold process startup, fresh/backing thread creation, per-turn updates, resume/reload, multi-root/additional-directory handling, Agent Merge, and fork paths. The PR adds fixed launch configuration and bounded in-memory profile/root mapping while preserving subprocess, filesystem, and IPC cardinality, cache lifecycle, and concurrency controls. No high-confidence actionable performance regression or qualifying performance regression fix was found.
